writing.label: Written by Roland Orzabal — not Gary Jules
trail: The song is credited to Roland Orzabal of Tears for Fears, who wrote it; the band recorded it first in 1982.

Gary Jules’ stripped-down 2001 version — used in Donnie Darko and a UK No. 1 — is, for a younger audience, the only version they know, so the song is taken to be his. He reinterpreted it; Orzabal wrote it.
The same page’s other story is the recording (above): Tears for Fears released it first, and the Jules cover eclipsed it for a new generation.

answer.label: Not a Gary Jules original — a 1982 Tears for Fears hit
answer.originalArtistDates: English pop band · formed 1981 in Bath
answer.sourceLine: For a whole generation, ‘Mad World’ is the desolate piano ballad from Donnie Darko — and they assume that is the original. It is not. The song was written by Roland Orzabal and first recorded by his band Tears for Fears in 1982, as an up-tempo synth-pop single that reached UK No. 3. Gary Jules and Michael Andrews stripped it down to voice and piano in 2000 for the film, and their version became the 2003 UK Christmas No. 1.

original.heading: Who recorded it first
original.label: Mercury Records (Phonogram)

original.charted: Reached No. 3 on the UK Singles Chart in November 1982 — the band’s first hit

trail: ‘Mad World’ was written by Roland Orzabal and first recorded by Tears for Fears, released as a single in September 1982 from their debut album The Hurting Wikipedia ↗.
The original is an up-tempo synth-pop record with a driving beat — a long way from the funereal version most people now picture. It reached No. 3 in the UK and became the band’s first chart hit.

In 2000, Michael Andrews and singer Gary Jules reworked it as a bare piano-and-voice arrangement for the film Donnie Darko. Released as a single in December 2003, it went to No. 1 and was the UK Christmas No. 1 that year — and for a younger audience, that slow version simply is the song SecondHandSongs ↗.

authors.name: Tears for Fears
authors.heading: About Tears for Fears
authors.metaLine: English pop band · formed 1981 in Bath
authors.bio: Tears for Fears — Roland Orzabal and Curt Smith — formed in Bath in 1981 and recorded ‘Mad World’ in 1982, with Smith on lead vocal and Orzabal as writer. It was their first hit, an up-tempo synth-pop single that reached UK No. 3. They went on to far bigger records like ‘Everybody Wants to Rule the World’, which is part of why their bleak little debut single got quietly re-attributed to the man who covered it two decades later.

authors.name: Gary Jules
authors.heading: Why it gets pinned on Gary Jules
authors.bio: Gary Jules (b. 1969) is an American singer-songwriter who sang the stripped-down ‘Mad World’ that his friend Michael Andrews arranged for Donnie Darko. Their voice-and-piano version is so different in mood from the 1982 record — and so tied to a film a younger audience grew up with — that many listeners never realise it is a cover at all. The version is genuinely theirs; the only error is thinking it came first.

authors.name: Roland Orzabal
authors.heading: About Roland Orzabal
authors.bio: Roland Orzabal (b. 1961) wrote ‘Mad World’ as one half of Tears for Fears, and it remained his song through every reinterpretation. When the Gary Jules cover topped the UK chart in 2003, it earned Orzabal a second Ivor Novello Award for a song he had written twenty-one years earlier — a reminder that the writer, not the famous performer, is the constant across all the versions.

misattribution.heading: The attribution problem
misattribution.intro: This is a generational misattribution: nothing about the Gary Jules version is wrong or fake. The only error is believing it is the original — a 2003 cover, tied to a much-loved film, mistaken for the source.

items.why: The Gary Jules and Michael Andrews version was recorded in 2000 and released in 2003. The song was written and first recorded eighteen years earlier, by Tears for Fears in 1982 the history ↗.
Their version is up-tempo synth-pop and reached UK No. 3 — a real hit, but sonically so unlike the slow cover that the two barely register as the same record to a casual listener.
Orzabal wrote the song and is a member of Tears for Fears; the 2003 cover won him an Ivor Novello Award. Authorship stayed put even as the famous performance changed hands.

misattribution.truthLine: Written by Roland Orzabal and first recorded by Tears for Fears in 1982, and made famous again — but not originated — by Gary Jules and Michael Andrews in 2003 the record ↗.

context.heading: Why the cover ate the original
lead: This is a cover-eclipse driven by mood and timing. Tears for Fears’ 1982 ‘Mad World’ was a hit, but it was up-tempo synth-pop; the 2000 reworking slowed it to a piano dirge and bound it to Donnie Darko, a film that became a defining cult object for the exact audience too young to remember the original.

The irony is that the two records feel like different songs. Because the cover changed the tone so completely — from restless new-wave to funereal ballad — younger listeners who meet the slow version first have no reason to suspect there was ever a faster, cheerier one that came twenty-one years earlier.
detailsBody: Roland Orzabal writes ‘Mad World’ for Tears for Fears.
Tears for Fears record and release it, September 1982 → UK No. 3, their first hit.
Michael Andrews and Gary Jules rework it as piano-and-voice for Donnie Darko, recorded 2000.
The cover is released as a single in December 2003 → UK No. 1, the Christmas No. 1 that year.
For a younger generation, the slow 2003 version becomes ‘the’ ‘Mad World’.
context.pull: The cover changed the tone so completely that younger listeners never suspect a faster original came first.
